title: An empty line after the last node of a document is counted by a keep scalar that ends the new document content
notes: The empty line before `---` belongs to the first document. A keep scalar at its end reads that line as part of its value, so `two` followed by that one empty line is the value `two` plus two line feeds, and no further empty line is written. The second document is not touched. The string with line breaks becomes a literal block scalar as for any new multi-line string member.

provenance.reference: Found by comparing random edits of random documents with a plain model while building a lossless document for a Python library.
